cards.a: A carbon alkyl, allyl, vinyl, or aryl magnesium halide (RMgX).

cards.q: In the classical Grignard reaction, what are Grignard reagents added to?
cards.a: The carbonyl groups of either an aldehyde or ketone.

cards.q: Under what conditions is the classical Grignard reaction carried out?
Which halogens can X represent in a Grignard reagent RMgX?
Why is the Grignard reaction important in organic synthesis?
cards.a: It is important for the formation of carbon–carbon bonds.

cards.q: Classically, what products does the Grignard reaction form from a ketone or aldehyde?
After whom is the Grignard reaction named?
cards.a: The French chemist François Auguste Victor Grignard (University of Nancy, France).

cards.q: In what year did Grignard describe Grignard reactions and reagents?
In what year was Grignard awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry?
Is the reaction of an organic halide with magnesium itself a Grignard reaction?
cards.a: No; it provides a Grignard reagent, but it is not a Grignard reaction.

cards.q: How does some chemists' broader definition of the Grignard reaction differ from the classical one?
cards.a: They take it to mean all reactions of any electrophiles with Grignard reagents, not only ketones and aldehydes.
